title.value: In Situ Construction of Cu<sup>1+</sup>/Cu<sup>0</sup> and Cu<sup>2+</sup>/Cu<sup>0</sup> Pairs of Cu-Based Catalysts for Electrocatalytic Nitrate Reduction.

abstract.value: Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction (NO<sub>3</sub>RR) as a sustainable nitrogen cycle regulation strategy provides a new pathway to achieve carbon neutrality goals. In this study, CuO, Cu<sub>2</sub>P<sub>2</sub>O<sub>7</sub> and Cu<sub>3</sub>(PO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>2</sub> (CuPO) are synthesized as pre-catalysts via a sol-gel process for NO<sub>3</sub>RR, in which CuO exhibits excellent NH<sub>3</sub> yields of 8.16 mg h<sup>-1</sup> mg<sub>cat</sub> <sup>-1</sup> (FE = 95.72%, -0.95 V vs. RHE) compared to Cu<sub>2</sub>P<sub>2</sub>O<sub>7</sub> (7.33 mg h<sup>-1</sup>mg<sub>cat</sub> <sup>-1</sup>, 94.88%) and Cu<sub>3</sub>(PO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>2</sub> (6.53 mg h<sup>-1</sup>mg<sub>cat</sub> <sup>-1</sup>, 92.04%). The combination of in situ Raman and XPS spectra reveal that the pre-catalyst surface is reconfigured to form stable active sites of Cu<sup>1+</sup>/Cu<sup>0</sup> (CuO-derived) and Cu<sup>2+</sup>/Cu<sup>0</sup> pairs (CuPO-derived) during the NO<sub>3</sub>RR process.
